location_desc: Spinosaurus fossils were found in the Kem Kem fossil beds of Morocco and Egypt in North Africa. It lived along large river systems in a hot, swampy environment during the Middle Cretaceous period.
fun_facts: Spinosaurus may have been the largest meat-eating dinosaur that ever lived — even bigger than T-Rex!
It had a tall sail or hump on its back made of long spines, possibly to help control its body temperature.
Spinosaurus spent a lot of time in water and was an expert fish-catcher — its nostrils were high up on its skull so it could breathe while half-submerged.
Its teeth were straight and cone-shaped, perfect for gripping slippery fish.
Scientists only discovered in 2020 that Spinosaurus had dense bones like a penguin, helping it dive underwater.

translations.title: Spinosaurus
translations.description: Spinosaurus was a massive fish-eating dinosaur with a dramatic sail on its back, and it may have been even bigger than T-Rex! Unlike most dinosaurs, it loved the water and was an expert swimmer, hunting giant fish in the rivers of ancient North Africa about 95 million years ago.

translations.title: Khủng Long Cánh Buồm
translations.description: Spinosaurus là loài khủng long khổng lồ ăn cá với cái buồm ấn tượng trên lưng, và nó có thể còn to hơn cả T-Rex! Khác với hầu hết các loài khủng long, nó thích nước và bơi rất giỏi, săn những con cá khổng lồ ở các con sông Bắc Phi cổ đại vào khoảng 95 triệu năm trước.
